BUSINESS TRAVEL TRENDS: WHAT'S CHANGING IN CORPORATE TRAVEL

Corporate travel is experiencing a significant transformation. According to a recent industry report, companies are increasingly prioritizing cost efficiency and employee well-being when booking business trips.

One notable trend is the rise of 'bleisure' travel — combining business with leisure. More than 40 percent of business travelers now extend their trips by at least one day to explore the destination. Employers generally support this practice, as it has been linked to higher employee satisfaction and reduced burnout.

Another major shift is the adoption of centralized travel management platforms. These digital tools allow HR and finance teams to monitor travel expenses in real time, enforce company travel policies, and reduce overall costs by up to 23 percent, according to industry data.

Despite the growth of virtual meetings, demand for in-person corporate travel remains strong, particularly for client meetings, training sessions, and team-building events.

EMPLOYEE SATISFACTION SURVEY — SUMMARY REPORT
Conducted by: HR Department, Vantage Consulting Group
Survey Period: January – February

A total of 248 employees participated in this year's satisfaction survey, representing 86% of the total workforce. The results indicate overall satisfaction has improved by 12% compared to last year.

Key Findings:
• 78% of employees reported being satisfied or very satisfied with their work-life balance.
• Only 52% expressed satisfaction with current internal communication practices.
• 91% of respondents agreed that their direct manager treats them with respect.
• The most commonly cited concern was lack of career advancement opportunities (mentioned by 44% of respondents).

Recommendations:
Based on these findings, the HR team recommends investing in improved communication channels and creating a formal mentorship and career development program.

A full report is available on the company intranet.

GREENLEAF ENTERPRISES
Expense Reimbursement Policy — Summary

Effective Date: January 1

Employees may submit expense claims for work-related expenses following these guidelines:

1. All claims must be submitted within 30 days of the expense being incurred.
2. Receipts are required for all expenses over $25.
3. Meal expenses are reimbursed up to $75 per day for domestic travel and $100 per day for international travel.
4. Hotel stays must be approved in advance by a department manager.
5. Personal expenses, entertainment, and alcohol are not eligible for reimbursement.

To submit a claim, complete the Expense Reimbursement Form (available on the HR portal) and attach all relevant receipts. Submit the completed form to your direct manager for approval, who will then forward it to Accounts Payable.

Reimbursements are processed within 10 business days of approval.

SUMMIT CITY TRANSIT AUTHORITY
Public Notice: Downtown Line Extension Opening

The Summit City Transit Authority (SCTA) is pleased to announce that the long-awaited Downtown Line extension will officially open to the public on September 15. The extension adds four new stations — Riverside, Commerce Park, University Hill, and Central Square — to the existing network.

The new stations will operate from 5:30 AM to 11:30 PM on weekdays and from 7:00 AM to 11:00 PM on weekends. Fares for the new stations will follow the standard zone pricing.

To celebrate the opening, all rides on the new extension will be free of charge during the first weekend — September 15 and 16.

For route maps and timetables, visit www.summitcitytransit.gov or pick up a printed guide at any existing station.
